relatedSnapshot.title: Move deals through pipeline stages from Calendly event types
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

This is part 4 of ENG-14790, and the lowest-priority child: build it last. It gives each Calendly event type a rule that creates or moves the deal on booked, cancel and no-show, with no workflow to build. Rules are on by default, so a workspace gets a clean pipeline the day it connects.

## Problem

* Only AI SDR threads move a deal on a booking today, and they pick the stage by name: the first open stage containing "booked". Calendly bookings only link to an existing deal.
* The create-or-update-deal logic lives inside workflow steps. In the two workspaces that use it, 1,022 of 4,241 deal writes failed in 30 days.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Calendly booking recorded] --> B[NEW: find event type rule]
  B -- internal --> X[Skip]
  B --> C[NEW: find or create deal]
  C -- several open deals --> D[Hold for review]
  C --> E[NEW: move to mapped stage]
```

## What's included

1. **The rules table.** One row per Calendly event type, with a "same for all" row on top. Each row sets:
   * the meeting type;
   * the pipeline;
   * the stage on booked;
   * the stage on cancel;
   * the stage on no-show;
   * a switch for deal creation.

   New event types appear by themselves. Pre-fill the meeting type using any meeting type that already books through this event type (the link added in the "always book through Calendly" child), and let the user correct it.
2. **Defaults, on.** Pre-fill each row with:
   * the default pipeline;
   * its first open stage containing "booked", or else its second stage;
   * "back one stage" on cancel;
   * a stage named "no-show", if there is one.

   Rules are on for every event type that isn't internal.
3. **Deal matching that never duplicates.** Match the person by email, and reuse their open deal in the mapped pipeline. If they have several open deals, hold the booking for review in the health log and don't move anything. If they have none, create one.
4. **Lifecycle rules:**
   * A reschedule never moves a stage.
   * A cancel moves the deal back only while it's still in the booked stage.
   * On an AI SDR thread, a prospect's cancel goes to the rebook flow from ENG-14761.
5. **Owner.** Keep the existing deal owner. On a new deal, the Calendly host becomes the owner when we can match them to a user. Otherwise it stays unassigned, and the host is listed as unmatched.
6. **One shared deal service.** Move create-or-update-deal out of the workflow steps into a shared service, which the rules and the workflow steps both call.
7. **Intake answers** show on the meeting card.
8. **Activation tracking** for saving a rule, through the activation tracking skill.

## Out of scope

* Mapping intake answers onto custom fields. That's a later ticket if customers ask.
* Moving the sales team's existing workflows onto these rules.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14791.

## Done when

* A booking on a mapped event type creates or reuses the deal and moves it to the booked stage. A cancel moves it back only from the booked stage, and a no-show moves it to the no-show stage.
* A person with two open deals is held for review, and nothing moves.
* A reschedule moves nothing. Internal event types do nothing.
* The workflow steps use the shared deal service, and their existing tests still pass.
* The rules table passes browser QA for defaults, editing and the "same for all" row, and its PostHog event lands.

## Name 2 and rollback

* Release behind the same workspace flag as the rest of this master. Rules only act on bookings made after the workspace connects.
* Undo: switch the rules off. Deals that already moved keep their stage history, recorded with the "automation" actor.

## Implementation context

* Stage moves: `persistDeterministicStageMove` in deal-stage-transition.ts, with `withCrmStageActor`.
* Deal linking: `calendar-booking-deal-link.ts`. The workflow deal steps are `plugins/workflows/crm/steps/upsert-deal.ts` and `update-deal-stage.ts`.
* A suggested rules table: workspace, Calendly event type, meeting type, pipeline, and the three stages. Keep it as its own table, not as columns on meeting types.
* The "reuse the live deal, hold when several" behaviour already runs in the HT Calendly sync job (commit 0d66c09d in the CRM notes repo).
* Full detail: AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI-Generated Name 3 Invalid Pipeline Not Available in Workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
When creating a workflow with AI for the **Create Deal** action, the system automatically selects the **Sales Pipeline**, even when that pipeline is not available in the current workspace. As a result, the selected pipeline appears with an **"Unknown Pipeline"** tag. Instead of assigning a default or invalid pipeline, the AI should select a pipeline that exists within the user's workspace or leave the field unselected for the user to choose manually.

relatedSnapshot.title: Build supplier acquisition board
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

Name 4 board for managing the supplier acquisition pipeline visually. Uses Pipeline 1 (Supplier Closing) from P2.08 and the existing CRM deal infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Name 4 board view using Pipeline 1 from P2.08
- [ ] Cards show: supplier name, contact info (email/phone), product categories, last activity date, assigned team member
- [ ] Drag cards between stages
- [ ] Click card → detail sheet with full supplier info
- [ ] Quick-add: "+" button to add new supplier lead directly from board
- [ ] Filters: by product category, assigned member, date range
- [ ] Route: `/dashboard/[orgSlug]/crm/suppliers`

## Codebase Reference

* CRM pipeline: existing `pipeline` and `pipelineStage` tables, deal/contact tables
* Name 4: check if existing CRM has kanban view to reuse (look in `app/(saas)/dashboard/` for existing CRM routes)
* Drag and drop: `<mention>/sortable` (also used in store builder P1.92)
* Admin pages: `Page`/`PageHeader`/`PageBody` layout components
* Detail sheet: use `Sheet` component for deal detail panel
* URL state: `nuqs` for filter state in URL
* tRPC: existing CRM deal procedures for CRUD operations

## Implementation Steps

1. Create page at `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/crm/suppliers/page.tsx`
2. Fetch Supplier Closing pipeline and its stages via existing CRM tRPC procedures
3. Fetch deals belonging to this pipeline, grouped by stage
4. Build kanban columns from pipeline stages — each column header shows stage name, color, and deal count
5. Render deal cards within columns: supplier name, contact snippet, product categories (from deal custom fields), last activity date, assigned member avatar
6. Implement drag-and-drop between columns with `<mention>/sortable` — on drop, update deal's stage via tRPC mutation
7. Card click → open `Sheet` with full supplier detail: all contact info, notes, activity timeline, stage history
8. Quick-add button ("+") in each column header → opens Sheet with new deal form pre-set to that stage
9. Filter bar: product category dropdown, assigned member dropdown, date range picker — all synced to URL via `nuqs`

relatedSnapshot.title: Show the full pipeline move on a Deal
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Verified 2026-08-19 against origin/main c2ed730b4e.** The old and new pipeline names are already recorded on both move paths, so the tracking half is done and this is now a rendering fix. What actually blocks it is the UI, which strips every pipeline field before display. Startable now — it has no blockers of its own even though the parent is blocked.

## Goal

When a Deal moves, show both the old and new pipeline and stage in Activity.

## Already recorded — do not rebuild

`changes['Pipeline Name']` already carries `old` and `new` on both paths that can move a Deal between pipelines:

* `updateDeal` — apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/deal.ts:4481-4486. Predates this ticket; carried into the monorepo by f52334c256 (2026-05-22), originally from 00ca39a432.
* `updateDealPipelineBulk` — apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/deal.ts:5206-5213. Added by ed398bb0e2 on 2026-06-15, after this ticket was filed.

The bulk payload is already asserted in apps/web/tests/trpc/crm-deal-bulk-actions-router.test.ts:479-490.

No other mutation can produce a pipeline move: `updateDealStage` and `updateDealStageBulk` both reject cross-pipeline stage changes, at deal.ts:564, deal.ts:993 and deal.ts:5050.

## Why it still reads as untracked

The recorded pipeline never reaches the screen:

* `HIDDEN_DEAL_FIELDS` and `isDealFieldHidden` drop every key containing "pipeline" — apps/web/components/crm/shared/activity-stream/activity-row-detail.tsx:1863-1873, applied at :1968 and :2204.
* Both description strings name stages only — deal.ts:4497-4499 and deal.ts:1305-1307.
* `DealStageHistoryDetail` renders stage old/new and nothing else — activity-row-detail.tsx:2224.
* Batching coalesces `Stage Name` across a group but overwrites `Pipeline Name` with the last value — apps/web/components/crm/shared/activity-stream/helpers.tsx:453-465.

## Done when

* The change is clear even when both pipelines use the same stage name. `Stage Name` is keyed on stage id, not name (deal.ts:4470-4479), so such a move records `old === new` and today renders as "Discovery → Discovery" with no pipeline shown. The event itself is not dropped: helpers.tsx:196-219 hides an event only when *every* change is a no-op.
* The move appears once in the Deal's Activity history from either write site — `updateDeal` (deal.ts:4237) and `updateDealPipelineBulk` (deal.ts:5145) — and survives the 10-minute batching in helpers.tsx:391 without losing the starting pipeline.
* Automated tests and browser QA prove the before-and-after details are correct.

## Startability

This is the only child of ENG-12581 with no blockers of its own. ENG-12769 and ENG-12770 are both blocked by ENG-12253 and ENG-12252, as is ENG-12581 itself. This one can start independently.

relatedSnapshot.title: Match payments to deals across a product's sales area or several pipelines, not one fixed pipeline
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

In Payments settings a product can be tied to one deal pipeline. Imported payments for that product only match a deal in that pipeline, and paid deals are only marked won there. A workspace that splits one pipeline into several loses automatic matching for every buyer whose deal sits in a new pipeline. This change lets a product match deals across its sales area, or across several chosen pipelines. Workspaces that leave their settings alone see no change.

Initial scope, subject to refinement during planning and review.

## Problem

* The AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace is splitting its HT / VSL pipeline into High Ticket VSL, Name 5, Outbound, Organic and Backend HT. Its seven High Ticket products are each tied to HT / VSL only. A payment imported from Whop for a buyer whose deal is in a new pipeline is left in Unmatched payments. It has no deal and no closer, and its cash is not counted in reports until someone assigns it by hand.
* A product with no pipeline set matches the buyer's newest open deal in any pipeline. In September that put about $119k of cash on deals in the wrong pipeline, for example Low Ticket instalments landing on a newer Backend deal.

## User experience

An owner or admin opens CRM settings, Payments, Products. On each product row:

* The pipeline control lets them choose several pipelines, not only one. Nothing chosen still reads "Any pipeline".
* A new switch, "Prefer deals in this product's sales area", sits in the same picker wherever Floor Command sales areas are available. It has no effect until the product has a cash category.

Both start empty or off. Changes are saved when the picker closes; Escape closes it without saving. When a payment cannot be matched because more than one deal fits, it appears in Unmatched payments with the reason "Several deals match", and a person picks the deal. Until then its cash is not counted, as with any unmatched imported payment.

## What's included

* Several deal pipelines per product, and the sales area switch, in Payments settings.
* The same rule applied everywhere the product's pipeline is used today: imported payment matching, the product check on manual assignment, marking a deal won on payment (live and in the past auto-win review), and the checks that keep a product's pipelines and its sales area consistent.
* A clear reason on unmatched payments when several deals fit.
* Not included: changing production settings for any workspace. The values for AI Acquisition are listed below and are applied only on James's go-ahead.
* Not included: the "Find Deal for Payment" workflow step. It never used the product's pipeline: it already looks across all pipelines and returns one open deal or asks for review.
* Not included: moving or re-pointing past payments. The deal and closer recorded on a payment at the time stay as they are.

## How it should work

* **Nothing chosen, switch off:** as today. The buyer's newest open deal in any pipeline, or the newest closed one when none is open.
* **One pipeline chosen, switch off:** as today. The newest open deal in that pipeline.
* **Several pipelines chosen:** only deals in those pipelines can match. The payment matches when exactly one deal fits: the buyer's one open deal, or their one closed deal when none is open. Two or more equally good deals means no match.
* **Switch on:** deals are considered in this order: an open deal in the product's sales area, a closed deal in that area, an open deal elsewhere, a closed deal elsewhere. The first group that has any deal decides. One deal in that group matches; two or more means no match. If pipelines are also chosen, "elsewhere" is limited to them.
* **Switch on, but the product has no cash category or its sales area has no pipelines:** behaves as if the switch were off.
* A chosen pipeline that has since been deleted stops automatic matching for that product, as a single deleted pipeline does today. It stays on the product, shown as unavailable, until someone removes it. Other edits to the product still save.
* One pipeline is saved exactly as before. Several are saved as a list, with one of them also kept as the single pipeline, so an older version of the app narrows to that pipeline and never widens to any pipeline. The list is stored with that pipeline first and only counts while the single pipeline still equals it: if an older version of the app later changes the product's single pipeline (to another pipeline, another member of the list, or none), that newer choice wins over the stale list.
* A settings page that was opened before this change cannot overwrite a pipeline list. Its save is refused with a message to reload.
* A workspace-wide pipeline limit on the Whop connection still applies on top. Inside that limit, a product with several pipelines or the switch on uses the same one-clear-deal rule; any other product keeps today's rule.
* A payment with no buyer email keeps today's rule: it matches only when exactly one deal sells that product, now within the chosen pipelines. The sales area order is not applied to it, because there is no buyer to check a deal against.
* **Won on payment:** a payment can mark a deal won when the deal's pipeline is one of the product's chosen pipelines, or, with the switch on and nothing chosen, a pipeline in the product's sales area. A product with neither stays ineligible, as today.
* When a product has a cash category and pipelines are chosen, at least one chosen pipeline must be in the product's sales area. For one pipeline this is today's rule.

## Who can do what

Workspace owners and admins change these settings, as today. Everything is scoped to one workspace.

## Done when

* A product with the switch on and no pipeline chosen matches the buyer's deal in any pipeline of its sales area, preferring an open deal there. Covered by tests for: one deal in the area; deals inside and outside the area; two deals in the area (no match, with the reason); no sales area set up (today's behaviour).
* A workspace with one pipeline chosen on a product behaves exactly as before, covered by a test.
* A product with several pipelines chosen matches only when one deal fits, covered by tests.
* A product with no pipelines and the switch off is never marked won on payment, as today, covered by a test.
* AI Acquisition's seven High Ticket products can be set so payments match deals in High Ticket VSL, Name 5, Outbound, Organic and Backend HT, using the values below.
* Product activation tracking is considered for the settings change and the decision recorded on the pull request.

## Open questions

* **Switch or automatic?** The brief described sales area matching as automatic for any product with no pipeline. Recommended and built as a per-product switch, off by default. Reason: replaying the new rule over AI Acquisition's last 30 days of imported payments (3,828) leaves 78% on the same deal, moves 15% to a different deal and sends 7% (270 payments, about $632k) to review. A payment waiting for review is not counted as cash until someone picks its deal, so that is too large a change to switch on for every product at once, and the standing rule is that a fix for one customer lands as a setting.

## Implementation context

**Settings for AI Acquisition Sales Team (not applied yet)**

For each of these seven products: Accelerator 2.0 HT, Custom AI Name 6 + DFY HT, Custom AI Name 6 HT, Name 9 2.0 HT, Name 7 2.0 HT, PS AI Name 8 + DFY HT, PS AI Name 8 HT.

* Deal pipelines, all five:
  * HT / VSL Closer Pipeline `<uuid>`
  * Name 5 `<uuid>`
  * Outbound `<uuid>`
  * Organic `<uuid>`
  * Backend HT `<uuid>`
* Prefer deals in this product's sales area: off. With five pipelines chosen, a buyer with one open deal across them matches, and anything else goes to review.

Backend HT is not in any sales area today, so the sales area switch alone could not reach it. That is why these products use the pipeline list.

Checked read-only on 2 Oct 2026, after the new pipelines went live: all five pipelines exist; all seven products are still tied to HT / VSL Closer Pipeline and sit in the HT sales area, which now holds HT / VSL, Name 5, Outbound and Organic.

How to apply, once approved: in Settings, Payments, Products, tick the five pipelines on each of the seven products and leave the switch off. The app keeps HT / VSL as the fallback pipeline by itself. If the values are ever written directly to the database instead, keep `default_deal_pipeline_id` as HT / VSL and store `deal_pipeline_ids` with HT / VSL first, or the list is ignored.

**Evidence, read-only, 2 Oct 2026**

* Two workspaces have a pipeline set on products today (16 products). Their behaviour must not change.
* Only AI Acquisition has sales areas with products mapped to them (46 products, 39 with no pipeline set).
* No workspace uses the connection-level pipeline limit. One workspace has won-on-payment switched on with no pipeline set on any product, so it wins nothing today and must keep winning nothing.
* 0 of 91 High Ticket and Outbound payments between 1 Sep and 1 Oct 2026 arrived through the import matcher, so the interim risk for the pipeline split is low.
* The replay uses current deal state, so it is an estimate.

**Risk**

Adds two columns to the product settings table, both with defaults, so the running app is unaffected during deploy. Rollback is a code revert; the columns can stay.

relatedSnapshot.title: Build CRM pipeline templates for e-commerce partner
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

The e-commerce partner needs 2 CRM pipelines: one for closing supplier deals, one for tracking store acquisitions. These are auto-created when the commerce feature is first enabled, using the existing CRM pipeline infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pipeline 1 — Supplier Closing:
  - Stages: Lead → Outreach → Negotiation → Sample → Agreement → Name 10
  - Default stage colors and icons
- [ ] Pipeline 2 — Store Deals:
  - Stages: Discovered → In Talks → Due Diligence → Closing → Acquired
  - Default stage colors and icons
- [ ] Auto-create both pipelines when commerce feature is first enabled for an org
- [ ] Use existing CRM pipeline infrastructure (existing `pipeline` and `pipelineStage` tables)
- [ ] Pre-fill with sensible default properties per stage

## Codebase Reference

* CRM pipeline: existing `pipeline` and `pipelineStage` tables in DB schema
* Schema: look for pipeline-related tables in `lib/db/schema/`
* Auto-creation trigger: could be an Inngest event when COMMERCE feature flag is enabled, or a check-on-first-access pattern
* Feature flags: `lib/features.ts` — `FEATURES.COMMERCE`

## Implementation Steps

1. Define pipeline templates as constants:

   ```typescript
   const SUPPLIER_PIPELINE = {
     name: 'Supplier Closing',
     stages: [
       { name: 'Lead', order: 0, color: '#6B7280' },
       { name: 'Outreach', order: 1, color: '#3B82F6' },
       { name: 'Negotiation', order: 2, color: '#F59E0B' },
       { name: 'Sample', order: 3, color: '#8B5CF6' },
       { name: 'Agreement', order: 4, color: '#10B981' },
       { name: 'Name 10', order: 5, color: '#059669' },
     ],
   };
   ```
2. Create initialization function: `initializeCommercePipelines(organizationId)` — check if pipelines already exist for org, create if not
3. Trigger: call on first access to commerce features — add a check in the commerce tRPC router middleware or a dedicated initialization procedure
4. Use existing CRM pipeline CRUD (insert into `pipeline` and `pipelineStage` tables)
5. Set default properties per stage (e.g., expected close date offset, probability percentage if applicable)

relatedSnapshot.title: Add public API pipelines resource
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

Expose CRM pipeline structure through the Public API so external clients can map deals to pipeline stages and read the available sales process. Pipelines should come before public deal writes if deal creation needs valid pipeline/stage IDs.

## Scope

Add workspace-scoped Pipelines endpoints under v1:

* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipelines`
* `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipelines`
* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipelines/{pipelineId}`
* `PATCH /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipelines/{pipelineId}`
* `DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipelines/{pipelineId}`
* Include stages in the pipeline representation, or add nested stage endpoints if the implementation review shows that is cleaner.

## API design

* Route resource name should be `pipelines`.
* Require bearer auth, workspace access, Public API feature gate, and pipeline-specific API permissions.
* Public response shape should expose stable fields: id, workspaceId, name, dealProbability, displayOrder, isActive, stages, createdAt, updatedAt, links.
* Stage shape should expose id, name, probability, displayOrder, isWonStage, isLostStage.
* Use cursor pagination for list.
* Soft-delete on DELETE.

## Implementation notes

* Follow the CRM resource pattern from Contacts/Companies.
* Add `apps/api/src/schemas/pipelines.ts`.
* Add `apps/api/src/repositories/public-api-pipelines.ts`.
* Add `apps/api/src/routes/v1/pipelines.ts` and mount under `workspaces/{workspaceId}`.
* Evaluate apps/web pipeline logic to avoid duplicating stage invariants.
* Be careful with won/lost stage constraints and duplicate pipeline/stage names.

## Tests

* Route tests for list/create/get/update/delete and stage representation.
* Repository tests for org scoping, soft-delete filtering, cursor pagination, unique-name conflicts, and stage constraints.
* OpenAPI assertions and real HTTP smoke coverage where available.

## Acceptance criteria

* Pipelines can be listed, created, retrieved, updated, and soft-deleted through the Public API.
* Stage data is represented consistently and safely.
* Cross-workspace access is impossible.
* Tests pass: API unit tests, DB/repository tests, typecheck, and API build.
* PR includes an `ai_context` block and links this Name 11 issue.
* One PR only, no co-author trailer.

**Preview:** <url:add-public-api-pipelines-resource-aiacquisition.vercel.app> — PR #4194

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix AI SDR issues with CRM stage categorization and calendar sync
relatedSnapshot.description:
This report currently combines multiple issues affecting AI SDR + CRM behavior. They should be tracked separately during triage, even if they later turn out to share root causes.

### Reported bugs

#### 1\. CRM stage miscategorization

Prospects are being placed into incorrect CRM stages.

Example reported:

* Name 12 appears as booked in the CRM, and the email thread reads like a call was confirmed, but there is no corresponding event on the calendar.

Impact:

* The CRM cannot be trusted as the source of truth for who is actually booked.
* Manual review is required to catch incorrect stages and avoid missed follow-up.

#### 2\. Calendar sync gap \[no action needed\]

Appointments created by AI SDR appear in the CRM Appointments view but do not consistently sync to Name 13 Calendar.

This is likely due to a brief outage issue we had during this week.

#### 3\. AI SDR service availability issue \[no action needed\]

This is likely due to a brief outage issue we had during this week.

### Expected behavior

* CRM stages should accurately reflect conversation outcomes.
* Booked appointments shown in the CRM should also exist in the connected Name 13 Calendar.
* AI SDR should remain available during manual review and triage.

### Triage note

This issue should be reviewed as a bundled report containing at least three distinct problems:

* CRM stage categorization accuracy
* CRM-to-calendar sync reliability
* AI SDR availability / service stability

Keep this issue as the umbrella report for now and decide during triage whether to narrow its scope or split follow-up work later.

relatedSnapshot.title: The AI panel lists pipeline stages to people not allowed to see them
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Someone deliberately denied access to the sales pipeline can still read the full list of pipeline stages by opening the "Create with AI" panel.

## Problem

The permission covering pipelines and their stages is enforced on the pipelines screen. It is not enforced when the AI view builder assembles its context, and that context includes every pipeline stage by name.

So a rep on a restricted role opens the AI panel to build a view, and the stage list comes back with it. They cannot see stages anywhere else in the app, but they can read them all here.

This is not new and was not caused by any recent change.

## Proposed fix

Leave the stages out of what the AI panel is given when the person is not allowed to see them, along with any guidance that depends on stages.

The panel should still work. Someone without pipeline access can still build views, just not ones referring to stages.

## What's included

Both the AI view builder and its suggestions endpoint.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately. Should be sequenced with ENG-12518, which is the same policy where the filter runs rather than where it is written, and must give the same answer.

## How it should work

Denying pipeline access removes stages from the AI context rather than failing the whole request, so the panel degrades instead of breaking.

## Who can do what

This is the ticket: reading pipeline stage names, including through the AI panel, requires pipeline access.

## What the user sees

Someone without pipeline access can still use the AI panel and gets no stage-based suggestions. Everyone else sees no change.

## Done when

- [ ] The AI context contains no stage names for someone without pipeline access.
- [ ] The panel still works for them rather than failing entirely.
- [ ] Guidance that depends on stages is dropped along with the stages.
- [ ] Someone with pipeline access sees no change.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

The permission means what it says: no pipeline access means no way to read the stage list, by any route.

## Implementation context

Found during review of the AI filter reconciliation work and confirmed as pre-existing. That work fixed the equivalent gap it had introduced, by deleting a stage-options endpoint gated on the wrong permission and withholding the stage filter when the permission is absent. This ticket covers the path that predates it.

Prefer omitting the stage portion of the context over rejecting the request, so the panel stays usable for restricted roles.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add public API pipeline stages resource
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

Pipelines are now exposed through the Public API, but pipeline stages are still only embedded in pipeline responses. API consumers need a first-class stage resource so they can list, create, read, update, and delete stages directly, and so deal creation/update integrations can resolve valid `stageId` values without fetching every pipeline payload.

## Scope

Add workspace-scoped Pipeline Stages endpoints under v1:

* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipeline-stages`
* `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipeline-stages`
* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipeline-stages/{stageId}`
* `PATCH /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipeline-stages/{stageId}`
* `DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/pipeline-stages/{stageId}`

## API design

* Route resource name should be `pipeline-stages`.
* Stages must be workspace-scoped and validate that `pipelineId` belongs to the same workspace on create.
* `pipelineId` should be immutable on PATCH in v1 to avoid invalidating existing deal pipeline/stage consistency.
* List should support cursor pagination with opaque workspace-scoped cursors and an optional `pipelineId` query filter.
* Sorting should be deterministic and avoid unindexed computed sort keys. Use `pipelineId`, `displayOrder`, `name`, and `id` ordering.
* Response shape should include stable fields that exist in the current schema: `id`, `workspaceId`, `pipelineId`, `name`, `probability`, `displayOrder`, `isWonStage`, `isLostStage`, and `links`.
* Do not add a migration for timestamps in this PR. `crm_pipeline_stage` does not currently have `createdAt`/`updatedAt`; add those later only with an intentional schema migration.
* Create/update should preserve existing repository business rules where possible, including terminal stage constraints and duplicate stage-name handling.
* Delete should be a soft delete and should fail safely when active deals reference the stage or when deletion would remove the pipeline's last won or lost stage.

## Security and permissions

* Require bearer auth, workspace access, Public API feature access, and pipeline permissions.
* Read endpoints require `pipelines:read`.
* Write endpoints require `pipelines:write`.
* Keep public error envelopes consistent with the existing API.

## Tests

* Add route tests covering list/create/get/patch/delete, permission failures, cursor validation, workspace/query-scoped cursors, validation failures, duplicate name, referenced-stage delete failures, and OpenAPI registration.
* Add repository tests for stage list pagination cursor behavior, same-workspace pipeline validation, duplicate handling, update behavior, terminal-stage invariant protection, and soft-delete/reference behavior.
* Learn from prior Contacts/Companies/Pipelines/Deals bot comments: scope cursors to workspace/query, generate the next cursor from the last returned item, avoid schema migrations unless necessary, use soft-delete helpers, and do not introduce unindexed computed sorts.

relatedSnapshot.title: Floor Command v2, Sprint A: AI Acquisition data correct
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What this sprint is

The shortest path to Floor Command showing correct numbers for the AI Acquisition sales team. Everything here is a data-correctness fix or a piece of history capture that only starts recording the day it ships. Making all of this configurable for other customers is Sprint B (Waves 2 to 5 under ENG-13681) and waits.

Decided 11 September 2026: fix the data for us first, then refactor.

## What is wrong today, from the manager's seat

* Talk time reads 0s after a day of calls.
* A voicemail box picking up counts as a connect, so pickup rate reads 90% when reps know it is nearer 65%.
* Cash categories exist only for the LT set (Low ticket, VIP, Name 16, Payment support). HT cash has no categories and no product is tied to an area.
* Payments land in the wrong month, and an LT payment can attach itself to a newer HT deal for the same customer.
* Moving a closer between teams rewrites last month's totals. LT Sales dropped from $1.37M to $1.09M for the same 30 days after a roster change.
* Payment Support booked says "Metric not available yet" because stage-entry history does not cover the window.
* Nothing records who set a meeting, so the SDR views cannot show setter credit.
* Misclassified payments cannot be corrected because the review queue and override action were never built.

## Already in flight, finish first (James)

1. ENG-13627 configurable cash categories per area, and each Whop product mapped to its area. This is the HT categories fix. Draft PR open.
2. ENG-13633 HT bookings saved into the CRM. Without it the HT views have no bookings.
3. ENG-13664 reschedules as one meeting. In code review.

## Pickup order (Anuj)

Steps 3, 4 and 5 add nothing visible on the day they ship, but they only capture data from that day forward. Shipping them early means the clock on trustworthy history starts sooner.

| Order | Ticket | What it fixes for AI Acquisition | Size | Waits for |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | ENG-13682 | Talk time reads the right column; automation switch works; area picker in the filter row | ~400 lines | nothing |
| 2 | ENG-13683 | A connect means a person answered; voicemails counted as voicemails | two PRs | nothing |
| 3 | ENG-13697 | Team and area stamped on every sale, booking, call and message; membership history | ~2,000 lines | nothing |
| 4 | ENG-13698 | Stage-entry history for every deal (first PR); cohort funnel data (second PR, can slip to Sprint B) | two PRs | nothing |
| 5 | ENG-13670 then ENG-13671 | Member custom field, then record who set each meeting | two tickets | 13671 waits for 13670 |
| 6 | ENG-12854 | Needs review queue and manual category override on the payments table | ~450 lines | ENG-13627 merged |
| 7 | ENG-13403 | Payments in the month they succeeded; LT payments never attach to HT deals; previewed historical repair | large, own repair step | nothing |
| 8 | ENG-13705 | Roster modes per view, so moving a closer never rewrites history; areas filter SDR activity | ~1,200 lines | 3 |

One person: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Two people: one takes 1, 2, 7; the other takes 3, 4, 5, 6, 8.

## Settings only, no code

* LT Sales view: roster switched to all accessible reps with the LT Closer pipeline as the boundary, so cash credited to sellers no longer on the team stops disappearing. Interim until step 8 lands.
* Funnel section hidden on every view until the cohort funnel exists. The section toggle already exists in view config.
* Payment Support view built once Name 15 provides the Payment Support pipeline stages. This also stops Payment Support collected being widened on the all-pipelines LT SDR view.

## Done when

* Talk time, connects and pickup rate on the LT SDR and HT SDR views match a hand-checked sample of one rep's calls for one day.
* HT cash shows its own categories and every Whop product is mapped to an area.
* A payment that succeeded in September is counted in September, and an LT payment for a customer with a newer HT deal stays on the LT deal.
* Moving a closer between teams changes no historical total on the LT Sales or HT Sales views.
* Payment Support booked is available for a 30-day window.
* A booking on a setter call type records the setter automatically.
* A misclassified payment can be corrected from the payments table and the headline reconciles.

relatedSnapshot.title: Group pipelines and filter sales and cash reports
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let managers group existing pipelines under configurable reporting names such as LT and HT, then view existing sales/cash reports for Everything, one area or one pipeline.

## User experience

Workspace owners and admins create or rename a reporting group and assign existing pipelines. Report viewers select Everything, an area or a pipeline. Captured sales use the original sale pipeline, so moving an opportunity does not move its earlier sales or cash. Areas are reporting groups, and moving a pipeline to another group changes its rollup without changing underlying sale history. Explain this in settings.

## What's included

Minimal settings and filters on affected sales/cash reports, comparisons, details and exports. Reuse existing UI and server filtering, with the current activation tracking convention. Depends on ENG-12451 . Development may use fixtures initially, but final integration and browser QA depend on that PR. Merge sale history first, reporting groups second.

## Who can do what

Existing permissions remain unchanged. Owners/admins configure groups. A selection only narrows already authorized pipelines. Invalid groups, removed selections and empty authorized intersections never fall back to Everything.

## Agreed legacy LT classification

James confirmed older history in AI Acquisition Sales Team belongs to LT. An owner/admin can choose one group to include older sales and payments. This setting defaults off, is workspace-specific and does not depend on its name. Everything includes this history; individual pipeline filters exclude unknown original pipelines. Explain that the selected legacy group includes an older-history portion beyond its pipeline subtotals.

On 10 September James additionally approved a one-time current-owner seller baseline for existing completed LT sales, implemented in the preceding sale-history PR. Those saved seller/date/value assumptions stay fixed after reassignment or reopening. Ownerless and unsupported history remain unknown. This does not establish an original pipeline: both assumed and other legacy history continue using the explicit legacy-group classification. Existing payment-time seller attribution and permissions remain unchanged. No production setup is performed here.

## Done when

* Owners/admins can create and rename groups and assign pipelines.
* Everything, area and pipeline totals reconcile across summaries, comparisons, details and exports, with the disclosed legacy portion.
* Original pipeline attribution survives opportunity moves; re-grouping changes rollups while preserving sale/payment history.
* Assumed legacy LT sales retain their saved seller and appear only in Everything or the designated legacy group, never by guessing an original pipeline.
* Invalid or unauthorized selections never broaden results; loading cannot show old totals under a new selection.
* Single-pipeline workspaces and arbitrary group names work.
* Focused tests, reviews and combined current-commit browser QA pass; activation evidence is reported accurately.

## Replacement decision

This reduced scope supersedes the old attached plan and closed Acquisity/Acquisity#6334 . Preserve old artifacts as history only. Excluded: area grants/security boundaries, People/dialer changes, all-channel activity attribution, email recovery/composer work, generic workflow refactors, retry infrastructure, historical area-version tracking, combined activation frameworks, unrelated production repairs and provider/billable operations. Related tickets are not additional requirements. No merge or production execution is authorized.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add ability to mark pipeline stages as "Won Stage" and "Lost Stage"
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Currently, there's no deterministic way to identify which stages in a pipeline represent won or lost deals. This makes it difficult to accurately calculate metrics like cash collected in the OS dashboard.

## Long-term Solution

Implement functionality to allow marking specific stages in pipelines:

* Allow 1 stage to be marked as "Won Stage"
* Allow 1 stage to be marked as "Lost Stage"

## Requirements

* When creating a new pipeline, require at least 2 stages marked as Won and Lost before saving
* Cannot remove these marks, only move them to another stage
* Provides deterministic way to identify critical stages across all custom pipelines
* Update operating system with updated values

## Context

This addresses issues with the OS dashboard not being able to accurately track cash collected. The short-term solution uses fuzzy matching (similar to what Mahmut implemented for deal value calculation), but this long-term approach ensures accuracy across custom pipelines.

relatedSnapshot.title: Tag Calendly booked deals with their event link across sales pipelines
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

For every Calendly booking that creates or matches a CRM deal, add the event type's scheduling-link slug to that deal's tags. Preserve its other tags and make repeated bookings and replays idempotent. Apply this to AI Acquisition Sales Team booking workflows across HT/VSL, LT, Consultancy, Follow-Up and Payment Support pipelines.

## Problem

Today's booking workflows receive a Calendly event type URI (HT) or an event URI/name (other pipelines). The `crm/upsert-deal` action in `fill-empty` mode skips `tags` when a matched deal already has tags. Some workflows have no slug source at all. As a result, the link used to book a deal cannot be reliably reported across pipelines.

## User experience

A deal booked from `calendly.com/<handle>/ai-business-strategy-call-ob2` carries `ai-business-strategy-call-ob2`; a deal booked from `.../ig-growth-call` carries `ig-growth-call`. A later booking through another event type adds its slug without removing existing tags or changing the deal's pipeline, stage, owner or history.

## What's included

* Resolve the canonical slug from the Calendly event type or scheduled event URI, including normalized webhook payloads that only contain the scheduled event URI. Reject missing or ambiguous slugs without inventing a tag.
* Append a slug atomically and idempotently to deals matched by active Calendly booking workflows in the Sales Team. Preserve all existing deal tags and the existing `fill-empty` behavior for other fields.
* Update the active booking workflows across the relevant pipelines to pass the resolved slug to their deal actions.
* Read back the published workflows and verify both a new deal and an already tagged matched deal. Include existing historical deals where a Calendly booking can be matched unambiguously to the deal. Dry-run counts by event type and pipeline first, preserve every existing tag, and skip ambiguous matches with a reviewable list.

## Done when

* New and matched deals across the active Calendly booking pipelines have the correct URL slug tag exactly once.
* Existing tags, stages, owners and pipeline assignments survive a repeat booking and replay.
* Unknown event types do not create an incorrect tag or deal mutation.
* Historical deals with an unambiguous Calendly booking gain the corresponding slug tag after a bounded dry run; ambiguous matches remain unchanged and are reported.
* Focused tests cover URI resolution, missing event type, append/idempotency and a matched deal with existing tags. Browser/provider QA confirms at least one real booking path.

## Implementation context

Current HT booking/cancellation workflow IDs: `<uuid>`, `<uuid>`. The other active booking workflows use `crm/upsert-deal` with `updateMode: fill-empty`. The existing server Calendly client is in `apps/web/lib/calendly/client.ts`; deal action is `apps/web/plugins/workflows/crm/steps/upsert-deal.ts`. The two reported organic bookings were recovered and read back on 24 Sep 2026.

relatedSnapshot.title: Let the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace store up to 1,000 CRM files
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Every workspace can store 100 regular CRM files. The AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace is moving off Close, and bringing over the 61 files attached to Close notes and deals would leave room for only 39 more uploads before the team sees "File limit reached". This raises the limit to 1,000 for that one workspace and keeps 100 for everyone else.

## Problem

Once a workspace holds 100 files, every upload in its Files tab fails with "File limit reached". The Close import stops at the limit too, so without this the Sales Team would hit the wall soon after go-live.

## User experience

* In the Sales Team workspace, the Files tab shows "X / 1,000 files used" and the upload dialog accepts files until 1,000.
* Every other workspace sees exactly what it sees today: "X / 100 files used" and the same limit message at 100.
* Text and email attachments still don't count toward the limit.

## What's included

* One per-workspace limit that both the upload check and the Files tab read, so what people see always matches what the server allows.
* The Sales Team workspace at 1,000. Every other workspace unchanged at 100.
* Not included: plan-based or admin-set limits. Changing a workspace's limit stays a small reviewed code change.

## Done when

- [ ] Uploads in the Sales Team workspace work past 100 files and stop at 1,000, with the limit message naming 1,000.
- [ ] Every other workspace still stops at 100 with today's message.
- [ ] The Files tab and upload dialog show the right limit for each workspace.
- [ ] Tests cover the limit decision for both the Sales Team workspace and another workspace, and a preview check confirms uploads are enforced at each limit.
- [ ] After release, the Close attachments import runs with its file cap set to match.

## Open questions

* Should every workspace get a higher limit instead? Recommended default: no. Keep this to the Sales Team workspace for now; a limit for all customers is a pricing and storage decision.

## Implementation context

* The upload check runs inside the upload transaction, under the workspace's upload lock, and counts only regular files (message attachments are excluded).
* Uses the same one-line reviewed allowlist pattern as the Conversations inbox read-path switch.
